title: Client Integration Dockyard — Standup Brief (Mar 12, 2026)
summary: Weekly radar for active customer onramps. Focus this week: Veridian Health cert rotation and firewall NAT, TideWater latency regression after quantized model rollout, BlueCove private VPC routing flakiness. Priority=Veridian (SLA), then TideWater (performance), then BlueCove (stability).
agenda: Quick wins / wins from last week
notes:
Opening: 15m sync to triage escalations; keep tactical items short.

Quick wins:
- Canary rollout for Veridian completed on test cluster; API contract stable.
- New smoke tests for SSO mapping merged (PR #64) — catches mapping miss on first-login.
- Autoscaling policy template updated to include burst override for Dedicated customers.

Customer: Veridian Health (Priority: P0 SLA window)
- Status: Data plane test traffic passed in dev, failing intermittently in staging during certificate rotation window.
- Symptom: During cert rotate, connections from Veridian's on-prem NAT intermittently fail TLS handshake, causing 503s for 30-120s.
- Root cause hypothesis: Veridian's firewall closes idle ephemeral ports early; our LB re-uses client-side ephemeral port and triggers mid-rotation state between old/new certs.
- Temporary mitigation: Increase client-side keepalive and push retry-policy with exponential backoff on the edge route for Veridian. Implemented as feature flag in routing rules.
- Permanent fix: Coordinate a one-hour maintenance window with Veridian to rotate certs in lockstep and adjust their NAT timeout; SRE to publish a zero-downtime cert-rotation playbook.
- Impact: Customer observed 4 incidents in last 48h; SLA breach window risk if not remediated.

Customer: TideWater Analytics (Priority: P1 performance regression)
- Status: After moving to quantized fp8-compatible variant, p50 latency increased from 82ms -> 135ms for short prompts (<=64 tokens). Throughput remains stable.
- Investigation notes: Profiling shows a higher kernel launch overhead with sequence packing for small batches on the selected kernel set. The quantized runtime is triggering a different attention kernel path that has per-invocation setup cost.
- Workarounds tried: (a) bump batching target to 4 for short prompts (reduced p50 to ~100ms), (b) revert to 16-bit model for low-latency route (recovered original numbers). Both are viable but cost/latency tradeoffs differ.
- Recommendation: Create a per-route policy that routes short prompt traffic to non-quantized instance and longer workloads to quantized to save cost. Product to approve policy change by EOD Fri.

Customer: BlueCove (Priority: P2 stability on Private VPC)
- Status: Packet loss spikes seen on VPC peering across us-west-2 when model cache warming occurs (KV cache prefetch bursts). Observed correlation: cache prefetch generates sustained outbound bandwidth that trips intermediary cloud NAT device.
- Mitigation: Throttle prefetch QPS and spread prefetch over 120s windows. Patch scheduled for canary tomorrow (03/13).
- Note: BlueCove asked for visibility into cache warming schedule — provide a CSV export for their infra team.

Cross-cutting technical items:
- KV cache migration: plan v2 (rolling warm) drafted. Key change: prefetch window + adaptive backoff to avoid peaking network. Plan in Confluence-4321.
- Dedicated capacity: one pool shows noisy neighbor behavior during nightly batch jobs — SRE to limit maintenance job concurrency on those nodes.
- Observability: Add token-level trace tag for customer_id to speed triage in Console. Low-risk change, request to product for prioritization.

Decisions made:
- Approve temporary routing rule for TideWater to send short prompts to 16-bit instances (owner: Priya).
- Proceed with staged prefetch throttle for BlueCove tomorrow (owner: Liam).
- Schedule Veridian cert-rotation maintenance with customer for Wed 03/17 02:00–03:00 UTC (owner: Ava to coordinate).

Open questions:
- Can product greenlight per-route model variant policies as permanent config? (impacts pricing and billing metrics)
- Should we expose cache-warm schedule API to customers or only CSV export? (security implications)

Risk summary:
- Veridian: High (SLA exposure) — mitigation requires customer coordination.
- TideWater: Medium (degraded latency) — routing policy mitigates in short term.
- BlueCove: Low-Medium (stability under cache warm) — patch scheduled.

Tone/notes to team: Keep customer comms tight and set expectations on timeline. Use #onramp-veridian for live updates during the maintenance window.
